session_covered: US and European sessions of Wednesday 11 November 2026 (US Treasury market closed for Veterans Day)
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Wednesday 11 November 2026; the US Treasury market was closed for Veterans Day, so bond yields are unchanged from Tuesday. This is a late retry run: SPI futures quotes span two sources and contract months and are marked approximate (see footnotes).

US bond market closed Wednesday for Veterans Day; the US 10-year is quoted around 5.00% (Yahoo 4.998%, Trading Economics 4.99%) with no Wednesday move to report - FNArena's +0.30% is a carry-over from Tuesday.

AUD/USD per Yahoo Finance (prior close 0.6871); Trading Economics CFD showed 0.6843 (-0.34%). Brent per FNArena settlement; Trading Economics CFD showed 92.47 (+1.39%) after touching US$94.6 intraday. Spot gold per Trading Economics; FNArena showed US$3,984.23/oz (-1.15%). Iron ore per FNArena and Trading Economics, which agreed.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are quoted at 9,156, down 0.4-0.6%: FNArena shows -37 points (-0.40%) and the TradingView December contract -0.57%. The prior ASX 200 cash close was 9,153.20 (+0.27% on Wednesday). Applying the futures range to that close implies an open of about 9,101-9,117, roughly 44 points or 0.48% lower, near 9,109 at the midpoint. The quotes span contract months and pre-open timing, so treat the level as approximate.

local_events: No scheduled Australian data releases or RBA speeches were listed for Thursday.
Earnings due: Xero (1H27), Aristocrat Leisure, GrainCorp, Orica, Paladin Energy.
ASX AGMs: AMR, CHC, CPU, CTD, GYG and others.
what_moved: The AI trade roared back overnight: strength in artificial-intelligence names, led by CoreWeave, lifted the NASDAQ Composite 1.60% and the S&P 500 1.31%, even as the US dollar index hit a 19-month high at 102.93 and markets pushed December Fed-hike odds toward 90-100%. The hawkish tone kept spot gold under US$4,000/oz (-1.2%) and the Australian dollar at US$0.6844, while Brent held above US$92/bbl on Middle East security concerns; sector-level S&P 500 moves were not available from the sources used. The US Treasury market was closed Wednesday for Veterans Day, so yields are unchanged from Tuesday.

news.headline: AI trade roars back on CoreWeave.
news.summary: CoreWeave-led strength in AI names lifted the NASDAQ Composite 1.60% and the S&P 500 1.31%, capping a risk-on session for US equities.

news.headline: Dollar hits a 19-month high; December hike odds near 90-100%.
news.summary: The US dollar index reached a 19-month high at 102.93 and markets pushed the odds of a December Fed rate hike toward 90-100%.

news.headline: Waller backs a 50 bp December hike.
news.summary: Fed Governor Waller signalled support for a 50 bp move in December if inflation keeps running hot, per reports.

news.headline: Gold falls under US$4,000.
news.summary: Spot gold dropped about 1.2% to around US$3,985/oz on the stronger dollar and higher rate-hike odds.

news.headline: Brent settles above US$92 on Middle East risk.
news.summary: Brent settled around US$92.7/bbl after touching US$94.6 intraday, as reports that Treasury Secretary Bessent was moved to a military base stoked security concerns.

news.headline: Anthropic IPO oversubscribed by up to US$1.4trn.
news.summary: The Anthropic Nasdaq listing expected next week is reportedly oversubscribed by up to US$1.4 trillion.

news.headline: Australian housing lending at a five-quarter low.
news.summary: Q3 Australian housing credit growth hit a five-quarter low, alongside soft consumer sentiment readings.

coming_up: The Fed's December meeting looms with a 50 bp hike now seen as increasingly likely, and the ECB has signalled a 25 bp move at its own December meeting. Anthropic's Nasdaq listing is expected next week; Nvidia reports earnings around 17 November.
